charts.annotation: Manufacturing's loss in FY2024-FY2025 was driven by the CDMO (biologics manufacturing) business, since divested; segment totals plus unallocated corporate costs reconcile to consolidated operating income.

charts.title: Net Income vs Free Cash Flow vs Owner FCF
charts.annotation: Owner FCF, where shown, is the DCF's series after SBC, interest income and lease principal.

balanceSheet.title: Balance sheet
balanceSheet.content:
Shareholders' equity is assets less liabilities; plotted against total liabilities to show leverage.

For Charles River Laboratories International, Inc.: equity that grows only through revaluations or share issues is not the same as retained earnings.

What to watch:

  • Liabilities growing faster than equity
  • Goodwill share of equity after acquisitions

cashDebt.title: Cash and debt
cashDebt.content:
Cash & equivalents against total borrowings (leases excluded unless noted).

For Charles River Laboratories International, Inc.: the DCF's net-debt bridge uses these balances at the latest balance-sheet date.

What to watch:

  • Net debt trend versus EBITDA
  • Refinancing dates and covenants in the filings

ebitda.title: EBITDA
ebitda.content:
EBITDA is earnings before interest, tax, depreciation and amortisation -- an operating-cash proxy that ignores capital intensity.

For Charles River Laboratories International, Inc.: read it beside CapEx: a business that must reinvest most of its EBITDA is not as cash-generative as the margin suggests.

What to watch:

  • EBITDA margin trend
  • Gap between EBITDA and operating cash flow (working capital)

epsDps.title: EPS and dividends
epsDps.content:
EPS is net income per share; DPS is the cash dividend paid per share. Both are in major currency units.

For Charles River Laboratories International, Inc.: the payout ratio (DPS / EPS) shows how much of earnings is returned versus reinvested.

What to watch:

  • EPS growth versus net income growth (dilution)
  • Dividends funded from earnings, not debt

fcf.title: Free cash flow
fcf.content:
Reported FCF is operating cash flow less capital expenditure. Owner FCF (from the DCF) further deducts stock-based compensation, interest income and lease principal -- the cash an owner could actually take out.

For Charles River Laboratories International, Inc.: the gap between net income and owner FCF is the earnings-quality question the valuation is built on.

What to watch:

  • FCF persistently below net income
  • Working-capital swings inflating one year's FCF

margins.title: Margins
margins.content:
Gross margin is revenue less cost of revenue; operating margin deducts operating expenses; net margin is after interest and tax.

For Charles River Laboratories International, Inc.: the spread between gross and operating margin is the cost of running the business; a widening spread with flat gross margin means opex is growing faster than sales.

What to watch:

  • Direction of operating margin over several years, not one
  • One-offs (impairments, disposals) that distort net margin

ocfCapex.title: Operating cash flow and CapEx
ocfCapex.content:
Operating cash flow is cash generated by operations; CapEx is cash invested in fixed and intangible assets.

For Charles River Laboratories International, Inc.: CapEx here is shown as stored (sign convention varies by ticker); the DCF splits it into stay-in-business and growth where disclosed.

What to watch:

  • CapEx rising faster than revenue
  • OCF that diverges from EBITDA

profit.title: Profit lines
profit.content:
Gross profit is revenue less cost of revenue; operating income deducts operating expenses; net income is after interest, tax and one-offs.

For Charles River Laboratories International, Inc.: the three lines together show where margin is made and lost between the top line and the bottom.

What to watch:

  • Operating income growing slower than gross profit (opex creep)
  • Net income far from operating income (interest, tax, one-offs)

revenue.title: Revenue
revenue.content:
Revenue is the top line: what customers paid for goods and services in the period, before any costs.

For Charles River Laboratories International, Inc.: the growth rate matters more than the level; compare it with the DCF's base-case growth path below.

What to watch:

  • Acceleration or deceleration in YoY growth
  • Whether growth is organic or acquired
  • Interim rows show seasonality

segmentRevenue.title: Segment revenue
segmentRevenue.content:
Charles River runs three reporting segments: DSA (Discovery and Safety Assessment, the preclinical CRO work -- the largest and most cyclical piece), RMS (Research Models and Services, research animals and related services -- the steadiest revenue base), and Manufacturing Solutions (CDMO/biologics testing and manufacturing support).

For Charles River Laboratories International, Inc.: DSA bookings and backlog lead DSA revenue by several quarters, so a DSA revenue slowdown here is a biotech-funding signal, not a company-specific one.

What to watch:

  • DSA revenue growth versus its own backlog trend
  • RMS as the defensive, less cyclical offset to DSA
  • Manufacturing Solutions' smaller, more volatile revenue base post-CDMO divestiture

segmentOperatingIncome.title: Segment operating income
segmentOperatingIncome.content:
Operating income by segment, plus unallocated corporate costs (shared services and corporate overhead not charged to a segment). The three segment lines plus unallocated corporate sum to consolidated operating income.

For Charles River Laboratories International, Inc.: Manufacturing Solutions ran a large operating loss in FY2024 and FY2025 -- driven by the CDMO (biologics manufacturing) business -- before that business was divested and the segment returned to profit in FY2026. DSA margin compression alongside flat-to-rising unallocated corporate costs is the second thing to watch.

What to watch:

  • Manufacturing's run-rate profitability now the loss-making CDMO unit is gone
  • DSA operating margin versus its revenue trend (pricing and utilisation)
  • Unallocated corporate costs growing faster than segment income

segmentBacklog.title: Segment backlog
segmentBacklog.content:
Backlog is unfulfilled client orders -- the forward order book. DSA backlog is the most closely watched because DSA work is booked and delivered over a multi-quarter lag, so backlog direction anticipates DSA revenue direction.

For Charles River Laboratories International, Inc.: DSA backlog has fallen every year since FY2022 as biotech/pharma clients pulled back preclinical spending; RMS backlog has been more stable. Manufacturing backlog is the smallest and least informative of the three given its recent portfolio change.

What to watch:

  • DSA backlog stabilising or re-accelerating (a leading indicator for DSA revenue)
  • Backlog coverage (backlog / trailing segment revenue) by segment
  • Annual-only data: backlog by segment is disclosed at FY, not quarterly

sbc.title: Stock-based compensation and share count
sbc.content:
Stock-based comp is the expense of equity awards; shares outstanding shows the dilution it causes net of buybacks.

For Charles River Laboratories International, Inc.: the DCF charges SBC as a cash cost and holds the share count flat, so this chart is the check on that assumption.

What to watch:

  • Share count rising while buybacks are advertised
  • SBC as a percentage of revenue
